title: Commission 014
summary: A full concourse-level restoration emphasizing mechanical purity and patina preservation.
story: Commission 014 arrived as a forgotten relic in a dusty barn. The goal wasn't just to rebuild it, but to resurrect its soul. We preserved the exterior patina while completely re-engineering the powertrain and chassis for modern reliability without sacrificing the analog driving experience.

sections.heading: Ownership History & Provenance
sections.text: Discovered in a temperature-controlled hangar in Geneva, Commission 014 arrived at our atelier as a matching-numbers rolling chassis. The vehicle had been off the road since 1989, preserved in a state of suspended animation by its second owner, a prominent Swiss horologist. The unbroken chain of ownership and original Swiss registration documents confirmed its elite status.

sections.heading: Restoration Milestones & Timeline
sections.text:
The project spanned 16 months of continuous labor, logged at 3,420 hours. 

• Month 1-2: Forensic teardown and chassis documentation.
• Month 3-5: Media blasting and structural metalwork.
• Month 6-9: Engine blueprinting and transaxle rebuild.
• Month 10-12: Wiring harness fabrication and interior trimming.
• Month 13-16: Final assembly, suspension tuning, and 500-mile shakedown.

sections.heading: Fabrication Photography & Metalwork
sections.text: Decades of exposure necessitated extensive structural intervention. The chassis was media-blasted to bare metal, revealing areas of oxidation in the longitudinals and suspension pickup points. Using factory-gauge steel and period-correct spot-welding techniques, we fabricated replacement panels that perfectly mimic the original factory seams. Every repair was lead-loaded, avoiding modern plastic fillers entirely.

sections.heading: Engine Rebuild Documentation
sections.text: The beating heart of the RS, the 2.7-liter mechanically injected flat-six, required microscopic precision. The magnesium case was completely cleaned, measured, and line-bored back to zero-hour tolerances. The mechanical fuel injection (MFI) pump was recalibrated on a specialized flow bench to match the original factory delivery curves. Every fastener, bracket, and linkage was replated in period-correct yellow zinc or black oxide.

sections.heading: Paint and Leather Specifications
sections.text: While the exterior patina was largely preserved and stabilized, the interior required a complete re-trim. We sourced authentic, correct-grain black leatherette from Germany, matching the exact weight and texture used in 1973. The seat inserts feature genuine Perlon corduroy, and the headliner was replaced with the correct ivory perforated vinyl. The tactile interface—the steering wheel and shift knob—was wrapped in full-grain leather, providing the exact grip required to command the unassisted front end.

sections.heading: Final Delivery & Valuation Statement
sections.text: Commission 014 was delivered to its new custodian in the fall of 2026. The vehicle was accompanied by a fully documented restoration dossier, authenticating every hour of labor and every replacement component. In its current state, it represents one of the most mechanically perfect, patina-preserved early 911s in existence. Independent appraisers have provided a conservative private valuation significantly exceeding the original build cost, cementing its status as an investment-grade artifact.
